title: A regular power quotient has its canonical short exact module presentation
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site essentially small in the coefficient universe, let $R$ be a commutative ring sheaf, and let $t$ be a global section whose multiplication on every $R(U)$ is injective. For $k\in\mathbb N$ let $B_k$ and $Q_k$ be the canonical ring power quotient and its restricted regular module [def-sp-regular-scalar-quotient-notation]. Then the canonical module sequence $0\to R\xrightarrow{t^{k+1}}R\xrightarrow{p_k}Q_k\to0$ is short exact, with $p_k$ the linear map induced by the specified ring quotient projection. Exactness includes the asserted zero composite, not a separately chosen projection.

proof.text: On each section ring, cancel t repeatedly to prove multiplication by t^(k+1) injective. Factor a linear map killed by this power uniquely through the sectionwise ideal quotient.

The sectionwise quotient maps into the underlying module of ring sheafification by a locally bijective map. The sheafification universal property descends the sectionwise factorizations uniquely to Q_k. This proves that the specified quotient projection is a cokernel; together with sectionwise injectivity this gives the asserted short exact sequence. The descended map is pinned by its formula on all quotient representatives.

theorem regularScalarQuotient_presentation
    (hregular : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Injective
      (fun x : R.obj.obj U ↦ (@id (R.obj.obj U) (t.val U)) * x)) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ hz : endoPow (globalSectionMultiplication R t) (k + 1) ≫
        ringMap (projection R t k) = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (endoPow (globalSectionMultiplication R t) (k + 1))
        (ringMap (projection R t k)) hz).ShortExact
